Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — really helpful. We're starting to map our regulatory requirements into the DPA and have a tight ask from audit: we need a documented process and SLA for an "emergency retain" window when Horizon invokes a legal or investigatory hold. Specifically:

- Maximum time to enact an emergency hold after a request (expectation: < 2 hours)
- How backup purges are paused while a hold is active (we need confirmation backups will be excluded from scheduled deletion)
- Log retention carve-outs (we produce ePHI access logs and need a 90-day short-term hold for investigations)
- Which subprocessors would be involved (we need a point of contact for any subprocessor that may receive retained snapshots)

I've attached a short requirements doc (Horizon_Retention_Reqs.pdf) with examples. Can Redwood confirm whether the hosted platform can meet a <2 hour enforceability SLA for emergency retains and describe the operational steps you would take?

Also interested in whether we need any DPA amendment language to make this explicit, and what typical lead time you need for a subprocessor attestation.

Appreciate a quick run-through — our procurement team (cc'd Carol) will use this to finalize contract language.

Best,
Alex
Director of Security Ops

Alex — thanks for the clear doc and for surfacing these requirements. High level: yes, we can support an "emergency retain" flow for hosted customers and will document it in the DPA amendment. Below is an operational summary and next steps; I'll loop in Legal (Kimberly) and Platform Ops (Karthik/Marissa) for detail.

Operational summary (high-level):
1) A customer-originated retain request is received (email + DocuSign) and routed to our Trust & Safety queue.
2) Platform executes a hold flag across active storage+backup indexes and updates retention metadata (this toggles eviction guards).
3) Any scheduled backup purge jobs skip objects marked with the retain flag; the retention flag persists until release authorization from the customer and Redwood Legal.
4) For logs, we can apply a short-term hold on the log ingestion index; we surface an export if requested for investigation.

Timing: Our staffed runbook supports an initial hold within 2 hours during weekday business hours (US PST). For after-hours we have an on-call triage process with a target 4-hour window for verification and action. We can propose SLA language that differentiates business-hour vs. 24/7 escalation.

Subprocessors & attestation: we maintain a current subprocessor list and can push an attestation or addendum for specific subprocessors. Kimberly — can Legal confirm typical attestation turnaround and any required changes to the DPA?

Next steps (proposed):
- Kimberly to propose DPA amendment language (we'll attach Redwood_DPA_Amendment_v1.docx).
- Karthik/Marissa to document the exact purge-pausing mechanism and expected audit evidence.
- I'll share DocuSign link for signature and route procurement questions (Carol).

Priya Natarajan
Trust & Safety, Redwood Inference

Folks — quick legal read and proposed language. Thanks Priya for the ops summary — that's exactly what we need to capture. Below are the items I'd like included in the DPA amendment and a short note on subprocessor attestation: 

1) Emergency retain initiation: customer submits an authorized request via DocuSign; Redwood acknowledges receipt within 2 business hours (define business hours) and confirms action within 4 hours for after-hours requests.

2) Purge pause: an immutable metadata flag will be applied to backups and snapshots to exclude them from scheduled deletion. Purge jobs will check the flag; any object flagged will be skipped until explicit release by customer + Redwood legal.

3) Log carve-outs: Redwood will support a temporary log retention extension of up to 90 days for investigation purposes. Such extensions are scoped per request and may be limited to specific indices/paths.

4) Subprocessors: Redwood will list subprocessors by function (storage, backups, logging/analytics). For any subprocessor that would access held artifacts, a targeted attestation is required before the hold is enacted. Standard attestation lead time: 5-10 business days; we can accelerate via prioritized SLAs for enterprise customers.

5) Evidence & audit trail: Redwood will provide a tamper-evident export (signed) documenting the hold time, objects flagged, subprocessor access events, and release authorization.

Draft clause excerpt (plain text):
"Upon receipt of a Customer Emergency Retain Request, Redwood will: (a) acknowledge receipt within two (2) business hours, (b) apply an immutable hold flag to the specified data objects such that they are excluded from scheduled deletion and purge operations, and (c) provide a signed audit export documenting hold scope and timeline. Temporary log retention extensions of up to ninety (90) days may be granted per request and limited in scope. Redwood shall notify Customer of any subprocessors that would access held objects and shall obtain or provide an attestation before such access occurs."

Karthik/Marissa: please confirm the short technical description of how we apply the flag and how purge jobs detect it — Alex needs assurance it's an operational hold (not just a ticket). Also, add any limitations or edge cases (e.g., offsite cold snapshots stored via third-party escrow).

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Alex / team — technical note from Platform Ops. Short version: we have a mechanism that sets a retention_mask metadata field at the object and snapshot layer in our storage index. Purge jobs consult retention_mask and will skip any object with an active retain flag. More detail below: 

- Invocation: our runbook provides a scripted action (authenticated API call) that flips the retention_mask for the customer namespace. The action is logged to an immutable audit stream.
- Backup purges: scheduled purge cluster jobs are idempotent and query retention_mask before deletion — if flagged they skip and emit an exception event included in the audit export.
- Cold/offsite snapshots: if an object was escrowed via our third-party archival partner, we surface a hold notification to that partner and request a temporary suspension of destruction. That partner has its own retention SLA and may require 24-72 hours to acknowledge; we will surface that window to the customer in the DPA note.
- Emergency SLA: we can commit to an internal target to apply the retain flag within two (2) hours during US PST business hours; after-hours target is 4 hours. We can instrument a monitoring metric (INF-7124) for this workflow.

Limitations / caveats:
1) If a customer requests a cross-region permanent deletion rollback, we may need coordination with the subprocessor handling cross-border replication — that can increase lead time.
2) For data already exported to a customer's own S3 (pull out), Redwood cannot retract those external copies — we will note that in the runbook.

I'll attach a short ops diagram in the Drive folder and update the INF-7124 ticket.

Karthik Iyer
Platform Operations, Redwood Inference
